items.title: WooCommerce AI-Shopping Readiness Checklist
items.description: A practical audit for making WooCommerce product data easier for search engines and shopping agents to understand.

sections.heading: 1. Confirm every product has stable, crawlable facts
paragraphs: Each product page should expose a stable title, canonical URL, price, currency, availability, image, description, SKU, brand, and variant information. Do not make essential product facts available only after a browser-only interaction.
Test several products, not just the homepage. Catalog quality is usually limited by the weakest product template or app integration.

sections.heading: 2. Validate Product and Offer structured data
paragraphs: Inspect the page source for Product JSON-LD. Confirm the Offer information matches what a shopper can actually buy, including currency, price, availability, and URL.
For variable products, make sure the structured data and visible page do not disagree about the selected variant.

sections.heading: 3. Make policies easy to locate
paragraphs: Shipping, returns, delivery timing, contact information, and geographic restrictions should be reachable through ordinary links and written in direct language. A shopping system cannot confidently recommend an item when the fulfillment terms are ambiguous.

sections.heading: 4. Check feed consistency
paragraphs: If you use a merchant feed, compare a sample of feed records with live product pages. Price, stock, identifiers, URLs, and variant attributes must stay synchronized.

sections.heading: 5. Run a repeatable audit
paragraphs: Record the exact evidence for every failed check. A useful readiness score should lead to a fix, not merely produce a number.

items.title: How to Audit Product JSON-LD Without Guessing
items.description: A field-by-field method for checking product structured data against the customer-visible offer.

sections.heading: Start with evidence, not a pass/fail badge
paragraphs: Extract every Product and Offer object from the rendered page and the original HTML. Keep the raw values so a developer can reproduce the finding.

sections.heading: Compare the fields that change a purchase decision
paragraphs: At minimum, compare name, URL, image, brand, SKU or GTIN, price, price currency, availability, seller, and variant attributes with the visible page.
A syntactically valid object can still be commercially wrong. A stale price or incorrect availability is more serious than a missing optional field.

sections.heading: Test multiple catalog states
paragraphs: Audit an in-stock item, an out-of-stock item, a discounted item, a variable product, and a product with multiple images. Template bugs often appear only in one state.

sections.heading: Create a repair order
paragraphs: Fix incorrect price and availability first, then identifiers and variants, then completeness improvements. Rank repairs by customer and revenue risk.

items.title: Make Shipping and Returns Easier for Shopping Agents to Understand
items.description: How to turn vague policy pages into clear, consistent purchase information.

sections.heading: Use one source of truth
paragraphs: Do not publish conflicting return windows or shipping thresholds across product pages, FAQs, checkout, and policy pages. Decide which system owns each value and update every presentation from that source.

sections.heading: State the decision facts directly
paragraphs: Include destinations served, processing time, delivery estimates, free-shipping thresholds, return window, item-condition requirements, fees, exclusions, and the actual return process.

sections.heading: Link policies from the product journey
paragraphs: A policy hidden only in a footer is technically present but commercially weak. Put concise policy summaries near the purchase decision and link to the full terms.

sections.heading: Monitor policy drift
paragraphs: Recheck policy pages after theme, logistics, marketplace, or app changes. The most damaging inconsistency is often introduced by an integration rather than a deliberate edit.

items.title: Why Product Variants Break Machine Understanding
items.description: A concise audit for size, color, material, SKU, price, image, and availability relationships.

sections.heading: A variant is a purchasable record, not just a label
paragraphs: Each purchasable combination should resolve to the correct identifiers, price, stock state, image, and URL behavior. A generic parent record is not enough when the actual offer changes by selection.

sections.heading: Look for silent mismatches
paragraphs: Common failures include a selected color with the parent image, an out-of-stock size marked available in structured data, duplicate SKUs, and price ranges that do not match the chosen option.

sections.heading: Test shareable states
paragraphs: When possible, a selected variant should have a stable URL or another reliable state representation. A shopper or agent should be able to return to the same purchasable configuration.

items.title: A White-Label AI-Commerce Audit Workflow for Agencies
items.description: A repeatable way for agencies to turn catalog evidence into prioritized client work.

sections.heading: Sample before you scan everything
paragraphs: Begin with representative product states and templates. A small evidence-rich sample reveals whether the problem is systemic before you spend time crawling the entire catalog.

sections.heading: Separate defects from opportunities
paragraphs: Label incorrect or contradictory commerce facts as defects. Label optional completeness improvements as opportunities. Clients should know which items create immediate risk.

sections.heading: Attach every recommendation to evidence
paragraphs: Include the affected URL, observed value, expected value, customer impact, probable source, repair owner, and verification method.

sections.heading: Sell implementation, not just diagnosis
paragraphs: A score alone is easy to commoditize. A scoped repair backlog, templates, regression checks, and monitoring create a defensible agency service.
